edition.title: AI daily — 31 October 2026
edition.lead: Wiz's 30 October report ties at least nine AI developer platform breaches in October to stolen model keys, with two stolen enterprise keys used for about 2.5 million model calls.
gaps: web_extract has no extraction backend configured, so these summaries rest on search snippets, reprints and company posts rather than full article pages.
No item dated 31 October was verified at a primary source. Roundup pages for that day list items I could not confirm, such as a DeepSeek V4.1-Flash update whose dates conflict, so I left them out.

stories.headline: Wiz links nine AI developer platform breaches in October to stolen model keys used for millions of calls
stories.summary: Wiz's 30 October report counts at least nine AI developer platforms that disclosed security incidents between 6 and 30 October, from Fireworks AI to Northflank. Attackers hunted stored environment variables, especially those granting AI access. Wiz followed two stolen enterprise Bedrock keys: the first test came within 30 minutes of the reported vendor-side credential access, and before the keys were remediated they were used for about 2.5 million model calls, which Wiz says likely cost over $100,000 at list price.
stories.action: Rotate model, cloud and Git keys that were stored on the listed platforms, not only AI keys, and check cloud provider logs for model calls from unfamiliar IPs.

details.label: Why it matters
details.text: Stolen keys were tested within about 30 minutes and then resold, so a vendor incident can turn into model-usage bills and data access within hours.

details.label: Caveat
details.text: Root causes are vendor statements as Wiz relays them. Crypto-theft and consumer-bill figures are anecdotal, and Wiz has not linked the resale operators to the initial breaches.

stories.blindspot: Mainstream tech press had not picked it up in the results I could see; the coverage is mostly Wiz's post and security-site reprints.

stories.headline: Google makes the Gemini API Computer Use tool generally available
stories.summary: Google's Gemini API changelog lists the Computer Use tool as generally available on 30 October, across the Interactions and GenerateContent APIs. The tool lets a model read screenshots of a browser, desktop or Android screen and propose UI actions that the application carries out. Coverage notes that execution safety and deployment testing remain the developer's responsibility.
stories.action: If you run browser or Android automation on Gemini, review the official execution-safety guidance before letting it run unattended.

details.label: Why it matters
details.text: Computer use moves from preview to a supported production tool, which makes agents that click through real interfaces easier for teams to justify.

stories.blindspot: Only the changelog and small tech blogs covered it in the results I could see.
